hook_text: Six paper squares and some tape. Fold them one way and you get a cube. Fold them another way and it falls apart.
clip_script: Six equal squares cut from card. Tape them in a cross: four in a column, one on each side of the second square. Fold the column round, flip the side squares in, and a cube closes with a click. Now tape six squares in a straight row and try again. The end squares pile on top of each other and one side stays open. Same squares, wrong net. Now one square and four triangles: tape a triangle to each side of the square, fold them up, tape the slanted edges. A square pyramid. Try it with three triangles and there is a gap. Try five and one has nowhere to go. Building proves the face list: a cube is six squares, a square pyramid is one square and four triangles. A tin is two circles and a rolled rectangle. And a ball? No flat pieces will ever close it without a gap.
visual_style: Whiteboard cube net folding up square by square; a straight row failing to close; a pyramid net rising to a point.
mood: Craft table, hands-on and a little triumphant.
pacing: The successful fold, the failed fold, the pyramid with the wrong counts, then the proof idea.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build a cube from six squares tonight, then try to find a second net that works.
